methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a logical, layered experimental design to support causal claims: bioinformatics discovery (TCGA-BRCA and GSE21653 ssGSEA), validation in a 120-patient TMA, functional loss/gain-of-function in 6 human and 2 murine cell lines, IFNγ perturbation, OT-1 SIINFEKL/H-2Kb coculture, in vivo orthotopic models in immunocompetent vs. nude mice with CD8 depletion and MHC-I blockade rescue, mechanistic co-IP/mass spectrometry, endosome isolation with RAB5/RAB7A, LAMP1 confocal colocalization, bafilomycin A1 treatment, adoptive T-cell transfer, and combination with anti–PD-L1. Controls are appropriate (sh-NC, MHC-I blockade rescue, IgG isotypes). Statistical methods (two-tailed t test, one-way ANOVA, two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni, Kaplan–Meier with log-rank) are appropriate, but no multiplicity correction across many bar-graph comparisons and sample sizes per in vivo experiment are not always explicit.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The findings identify TSPAN13 as a potentially druggable immune-evasion target in breast cancer, with preclinical evidence that TSPAN13 knockdown sensitizes tumors to anti–PD-L1 therapy. Clinical relevance is real but preclinical: TCGA correlations support prognostic signal, but no small-molecule inhibitor or antibody against TSPAN13 is tested. Oxford LoE maps to 5 (mechanistic/basic science).

reporting_quality.justification: As a mixed preclinical-human-tissue study with extensive animal work, ARRIVE is the applicable standard. IACUC approval (JDYY20240440), ethics approval (2023-395), strain details (RRIDs for C57BL/6J, BALB/c, BALB/c nude, OT-1, MMTV-PyMT), cell culture sources with RRIDs, antibody catalog numbers, housing (SPF), and randomization details are provided. Cell-line authentication and Mycoplasma testing are described. However, some items (exact group sizes in each experiment, randomization/blinding procedures, primary endpoint pre-specification) are only partially described, and no data availability or code sharing statement or accession number for RNA-seq is visible. TMA metadata is summarized but individual patient data are not accessible.

novelty_literature.justification: The specific claim that TSPAN13 acts as a negative regulator of surface MHC-I via STUB1-mediated ubiquitination and lysosomal degradation in breast cancer appears to be a novel mechanistic finding. STUB1's role in MHC-I quality control has been described (ref 16), and tetraspanins regulate membrane protein trafficking, but linking TSPAN13 specifically to MHC-I endocytosis and to anti–PD-L1 responsiveness is a meaningful, coherent advance. This is a first-in-class mechanistic finding in breast cancer immunology with translational implications.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized, progressing cleanly from bioinformatic discovery to mechanism to therapeutic combination. Figures 1–7 are informative and the flow between in vitro, in vivo, and mechanistic sections is clear. The Discussion acknowledges key limitations (no small-molecule inhibitor, focus on classical MHC-I). Minor issues include some repetitive phrasing across paragraphs and slightly inconsistent gene/protein formatting (TSPAN13 vs. Tspan13), but overall clarity is high.

key_strengths: Systematic mechanistic dissection linking TSPAN13 to STUB1-mediated MHC-I ubiquitination, endocytic trafficking (RAB5/RAB7A), and lysosomal (LAMP1/bafilomycin) degradation
Multi-model validation across 6 human and 2 murine breast cancer cell lines, 120-patient TMA, and orthotopic models in 4 mouse strains including CD8 depletion and MHC-I blockade rescue
Functional immunology readouts (OT-1 cocultures with CD69/IFNγ/GZMB/TNFα, SIINFEKL proliferation, ELISPOT, adoptive transfer) consistently supporting the central claim
Translational relevance demonstrated via TCIA immunophenoscore analysis and combination with anti–PD-L1 showing synergistic tumor suppression and survival extension
key_concerns: Human clinical relevance rests on TMA correlations (n=120) and TCGA; no prospective or patient-response data linking TSPAN13 to actual immunotherapy outcomes
All functional experiments use shRNA/siRNA knockdown; no small-molecule inhibitor or antibody against TSPAN13 is tested, limiting direct translational feasibility
Multiplicity not explicitly controlled across numerous bar-graph comparisons; some in vivo experiments lack clear group-size reporting
Data availability: no sequencing accession numbers or code repositories visible in provided text
Mechanism involves additional E3 ligases (acknowledged), leaving the full pathway incompletely mapped
chief_reviewer.rationale: Comprehensive and internally consistent mechanistic immuno-oncology study with multi-model validation and plausible therapeutic rationale; tier 2 acceptability with minor revisions to strengthen clinical translation and reporting standards.
